features.title: Activity feed
features.pitch: First version shipped as Sessions: a self-written daily log per project, kept by hooks and the agent. Next: a cross-project activity view.

features.title: "Since you last looked" briefing
features.pitch: Open Grimoire after a break and get a generated summary: cards moved, decisions made, files touched, what's waiting on you. The agent writes it from the activity feed and git.

features.title: Review lane
features.pitch: Agents finish work into a Review column with a diff summary; you approve or bounce from the board. Approval writes back, the agent sees it next turn. Human-in-the-loop without a chat transcript.

features.title: Git-aware repo view
features.pitch: Branch, recent commits, uncommitted changes and per-file diffs inside the repo view. Read-only git commands only.

features.title: Comments the agent can read
features.pitch: Select text in any artifact and leave a comment. It lands in _comments.json beside the artifact, so your agent picks it up and replies or fixes it. Review docs the way you review PRs.

features.title: Test + CI viewer
features.pitch: *.tests.json (or JUnit XML) renders as a pass/fail wall; a CI status file shows the last runs. The dashboard's health can read it.

features.title: Chart viewer
features.pitch: *.chart.json or a CSV with a sidecar spec renders as a themed chart. Agents stop hand-writing SVG.

features.title: Diagram viewer
features.pitch: Boxes-and-arrows from a tiny text format, themed and live. Architecture docs that redraw when the agent edits them.

features.title: Live dev-server tabs
features.pitch: A .link to localhost:3000 with a health dot, auto-reconnect and the server's log one click away. The running app sits beside its board and docs.

features.title: One channel per agent
features.pitch: When several agents work at once, each gets a channel showing its current task, files and questions. Mission control for multi-agent runs.

features.title: Daily standup artifact
features.pitch: Every morning the agent writes yesterday / today / blocked from the board, git and the activity feed. Shareable with a team as-is.

features.title: Questions inbox
features.pitch: Agents park questions in _questions.json instead of stopping. You answer from Grimoire, in any order; answers flow back as files.

features.title: Theme gallery + sharing
features.pitch: Browse, preview and install themes from a gallery; share yours as one CSS file. The fun on-ramp that gets people to try it.

features.title: Phone glance
features.pitch: A read-only tunnel with a token so you can check the board and activity from your phone while the agent works.

features.title: Editor panels
features.pitch: VS Code / JetBrains panel showing the current channel next to your code. Same server, no new concepts.

features.title: MCP server (optional)
features.pitch: For harnesses without good file tools: tv_create, tv_focus, tv_update tools that just write the same files. Files stay the source of truth.

items.text: `npx Grimoire init`: create .grimoire/, install the skill for Claude Code, Codex and others
Tests for the server, markdown renderer and write rules
Run on macOS, Linux and Windows; fix path edge cases
README with a 30-second demo GIF (theme switch + agent updating the board)
Put Grimoire on 3 real repos: Grimoire, deck, json-render-app
Ship the activity feed (f01): it's what makes agent work legible
Keep a diary in learnings.md: when did we open Grimoire, and when didn't we?
Measure: does the agent keep the board true without being asked?
Ship the questions inbox (f12) and comments (f05)
Show HN / r/ClaudeAI / agent Discords with the demo
Talk to 10 people who use coding agents daily; watch them install it
Reach out to Telepath (Television) — compare notes, maybe contribute upstream
Write the viewer spec v0.1 so others can build viewers
Decide: stay a free OSS tool, or build hosted sharing for teams
Go / pivot / park review against the kill criteria

names.name: Grimoire
names.note: Chosen Oct 2. A book of spells: skills are spells, artifacts are pages, sessions write the history. CLI: grim.

names.name: Glance
names.note: The early favourite: names the habit. Already used by a popular self-hosted dashboard.

names.name: Tome
names.note: Each project a tome. Strong and simple; an AI presentation startup uses it.

names.name: Lore
names.note: Everything a project knows. Great fit, shortlisted.

names.name: Quire
names.note: A gathering of pages bound into a book. Rare and exact.

names.name: tv
names.note: The working name, after Television. Retired: this idea is our own now.
